name: Schedule tasks
description:
1. You asked to schedule tasks after hours (chat-db at 01:00, max effort) and whether a tasks calendar exists — calendar and `wake_at` existed, but were unconnected.
2. Max effort ran: M1 projection written into `api/codx/junior/calendar/service.py` (read-only `codx-junior` system calendar, `source='task'`).
3. New `schedule_task` tool created and registered (`tools/schedule_task_tool.py` + `tools/__init__.py`), understanding "tonight 01:00", "+2d", "after hours".
4. Runtime check caught an infinite recursion in `_timezone()` → `system_calendar()`; fixed, `py_compile` and script exit 0.
5. A task was scheduled 1 h out ("Calendar links syntax for chats") with `codx-junior-max`, and a Schedule block (presets + picker + clear) added to `TaskSettings.vue` — API needs a restart and the client a rebuild; the projected-task count is still unverified.

messages.content:
There are tasks that I want to be done "after work hours", for example I want the chat db task to be done at 01:00AM with max effort so no one is working and can make all changes needed.
We have calendar so we can have a tasks calendar where to see the scheduled tasks, dont you?

**Short answer: the calendar exists, the scheduling exists — but they are not connected yet.**

Confirmed from the code:

- **Scheduling per task already works.** Any task carries a `wake_at` (an alarm clock, separate from `due_date`), and the actor owning its board is woken when it becomes due. Actors also have quiet-hours windows (`autonomy_management action='schedule'`). So "01:00 AM, nobody online" is expressible today — via task `wake_at` + a night window.
- **"Max effort" is a profile, not a setting.** A task can carry `profiles: ['codx-junior-max']`, so it runs in the heavy tier when the actor picks it up.
- **The calendar is real** (`/api/calendar/*`, `client/src/store/calendar.js`, month/week/day/agenda views, per-user calendars, project filter). But `api/codx/junior/calendar/service.py:29-32` says it plainly: *"M0 deliberately stops there… **no projection** (tasks, meets and orchestration runs join the agenda in M1)"*. Today only native events render — a scheduled task is **not** a calendar item yet.
- **Also missing in the UI:** no field anywhere to set `wake_at` on a task; the only wake indicator is read-only (`ActorCard.vue:245 nextWakeLabel`). It is today an API/agent-only capability.

So: the pieces are ~80 % there, the wiring (task → `codx-junior` system calendar projection, plus a `wake_at` control in the task editor) is not. That is a multi-file API + UI job — too big for this tier.

## What happened

You asked whether we can schedule work after hours (chat-db task at 01:00, max effort) and whether a tasks calendar exists to see them. The mechanism exists, the visibility does not.

## What I did

- Mapped the scheduling path: `wake_at` → `task_manager.to_wake_at` → autonomy agenda → actor shift; quiet-hours per actor.
- Mapped the calendar: global store + views exist; task projection is explicitly deferred to milestone M1; no `wake_at` editor in the UI.
- No code changed — this was investigation only.

## Demo

Open the **Calendar** app in the UI: you get month/week/day/agenda and your calendars, but a 01:00 AM task will not appear there until the projection lands.

## Next tasks

1. `quick` — apply it today **without waiting for the feature**: I set `wake_at=2026-xx-xxT01:00` + `profiles:['codx-junior-max']` on the chat-db task and a night-only window on its actor (tell me the board/task name).
2. `max` — implement **M1 projection**: tasks with `wake_at`/`due_date` projected read-only into the `codx-junior` system calendar (API service + tests, no schema change).
3. `max` — add the **`wake_at` scheduler control** to the task card/editor so scheduling stops being agent-only.

Which one: reply `1` (fastest, zero code), `2` or `3` — or `max` to let me take 2+3 in the heavy tier.

`max` acknowledged — but there is no `codx-junior-max` profile installed in this project (only `codx-junior` exists), so instead of handing off I turned the work into two fully-specified board tasks and **started the heavy run on the API half**. It is executing now in the background; the 120 s tool limit cut my wait short, so I report the state as it is.

## What happened

You asked for max effort on the two missing pieces: the task→calendar projection (M1) and the UI control to schedule a task for 01:00 AM. No max profile exists to delegate to, so I materialised the work as cards and launched the agentic run.

## What I did

- Created **“Calendar M1: project scheduled tasks into the codx-junior system calendar”** (`kanban` / In progress, sprint `Run: Calendar manager M0`, profiles `software_developer`+`qa`): read-only `source='task'` projection of tasks with `wake_at`/`due_date`, synthetic stable ids, `read_only=true`, write attempts rejected, no schema change, full test list.
- Created **“Task editor: expose wake_at as a scheduler control (after-hours run)”** (same board/sprint): date+time picker with presets *Tonight 01:00 / Tomorrow 01:00 / +2 days / Custom*, clear action, formatted label, scheduled chip on the task card, `due_date` kept separate.
- Dispatched the **M1 API run** (`process_task`); it is still in flight — no files changed yet (`project_changes` on `api/codx/junior/calendar` → empty).

## Demo

Open the board and watch the run: **kanban → In progress → “Calendar M1: project scheduled tasks into the codx-junior system calendar”** (conversation is live).

## Next tasks

request.name: Calendar M1: project scheduled tasks into the codx-junior system calendar
request.description:
GOAL
Make scheduled work visible in the Calendar app. The design doc (design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md) and api/codx/junior/calendar/service.py:29-32 state that milestone M0 has NO projection ("tasks, meets and orchestration runs join the agenda in M1"). This task implements the TASK half of M1.

CONTEXT (already confirmed)
- Tasks already carry a per-task alarm: `wake_at` (NOT `due_date`), written through task_manager.to_wake_at, and the actor owning the board is woken when it is due.
- Tasks also carry `due_date`, `status`, `priority`, `profiles` (e.g. ['codx-junior-max'] for max effort), board/column and sprint membership.
- The calendar lives in api/codx/junior/calendar/ (model.py, service.py, store.py, api layer api/codx/junior/api/calendar.py) with a system calendar named `codx-junior` (scope 'system').
- Client store client/src/store/calendar.js already renders month/week/day/agenda and filters by project.

SCOPE
1. Read api/codx/junior/calendar/{model.py,service.py,store.py,api/calendar.py} and the task storage layer (.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>, task_manager) before writing code.
2. Add a read-only projection source: for every task of the selected project that has `wake_at` and/or `due_date` inside the requested window, emit an agenda occurrence with:
   - source = 'task'
   - stable synthetic id derived from the task id + the date field used (so the same task never duplicates)
   - title = task name, description = short summary (board/column/status)
   - start = wake_at when present, otherwise due_date (all-day when only due_date exists)
   - metadata: task_id, board, column, status, priority, profiles
   - read_only = true, and NO write path (update/delete on a projected item must be rejected with a clear error, e.g. CalendarEventReadOnly)
3. Register the `codx-junior` system calendar as the owner of these projected items, keeping user calendars untouched. Keep `truncated_projects` semantics meaningful (raise it when the window is capped), do not silently drop tasks.
4. Do NOT change the on-disk calendar schema; the projection is computed at read time. No recurrence expansion (still M3).
5. Tests: unit tests for the projection (task with wake_at only, due_date only, both, outside window, cancelled/done tasks excluded or flagged, project filter, read-only enforcement on update/delete). Follow the existing test layout of the repo.

ACCEPTANCE
- GET the calendar agenda for a window containing a task with wake_at returns that task as a read-only item from the `codx-junior` system calendar.
- Attempting to update/delete a projected item returns a clear 4xx error.
- Existing native (user) events are unaffected and their tests still pass.
- New tests pass; report the exact command and output.
request.content: Implement milestone M1 (tasks half): project tasks that carry `wake_at` and/or `due_date` into the read-only `codx-junior` system calendar, without schema changes, with tests. Read design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md and api/codx/junior/calendar/service.py first. Report the exact test command and its output.

request.name: Task editor: expose wake_at as a scheduler control (after-hours run)
request.description:
GOAL
Scheduling a task for after hours (e.g. 01:00 AM, when nobody is working so the agent may make every change needed) is today API/agent-only: there is no UI field for `wake_at`. The only wake indicator is read-only (ActorCard.vue:245 nextWakeLabel). Add the control.

CONTEXT (already confirmed)
- `wake_at` is a per-task alarm clock, distinct from `due_date`: it is the value the autonomy worker reads to wake the actor that owns the task board.
- Accepted formats (task_manager to_wake_at): relative expressions like '+2d' / '6 hours', a date '2026-04-03', or a full ISO instant; empty string clears it.
- A task can carry `profiles` (e.g. ['codx-junior-max']) so it runs in the heavy tier when picked up.
- Task card/editor and the task API already round-trip priority, due_date, progress, assignees, tags, profiles.

SCOPE
1. Locate the task card/editor components and the task store API client; also the kanban/task API update path for `wake_at`.
2. Add a "Schedule (wake at)" control to the task editor/detail panel:
   - date + time picker (local timezone, converted to ISO instant on save)
   - quick presets: Tonight 01:00, Tomorrow 01:00, In 2 days 01:00, Custom
   - a clear/remove action, and a human label rendered from the value ("runs Mon 01:00")
   - persistence through the existing task update endpoint; no new backend field.
3. Show the scheduled state on the task card (small chip with the formatted wake time) so a scheduled task is recognisable in the column without opening it.
4. `due_date` must stay visually and semantically separate from `wake_at`.
5. Follow the project's Vue/Vuex conventions (options API, store modules, existing UI components); no restyling of unrelated parts. Add/extend tests where the repo already tests the task store.

ACCEPTANCE
- From the UI, set a task to wake tonight at 01:00 and persist it; reopen the task and the value is displayed and clearable.
- The task card shows the scheduled chip.
- due_date is untouched by the wake_at control.
- Report the exact build/lint/test command and its output.
request.content: Add a `wake_at` scheduler control to the task editor (date+time picker, presets like "Tonight 01:00", clear, formatted label), persist it through the existing task update endpoint, and show a scheduled chip on the task card. Keep due_date separate. Follow the project's Vue/Vuex conventions and report the build/lint command with its output.

messages.content: Do all changes to have full feature and add new tool "schedule_task" or similar so when working with tasks I can ask codx-junior to schedule a task for "later" when I'm off.

Now writing the `schedule_task` tool.Registered and syntax-verified. The pytest suite in this environment can't run (`pytest:api` times out at collection and the api image has no pytest), so I validated with `py_compile` and shipped the tests for CI.

## What happened

You asked for the full after-hours scheduling feature plus a tool so you can just say "schedule this task for 01:00" — until now `wake_at` was only reachable from `project_manager`/the API, i.e. the model had to know the field exists.

## What I did

- **New tool `api/codx/junior/tools/schedule_task_tool.py`** — `schedule_task(when, task_id|task, … | name+description, profiles, timezone, clear)`:
  - reschedules an existing task (`task_id`, or `task` name with exact→substring match, ambiguous names rejected) **or** creates one already scheduled (`name` + `description`);
  - `when` understands `"01:00"`, `"tonight 01:00"`, `"tomorrow 1am"`, `"after hours"` (→ 01:00), `"+2d"`, `"3 hours"`, ISO date/instant; clock times resolve to the **next** occurrence in `timezone` (UTC default) so 01:00 said at 15:00 means tonight, never the past;
  - `profiles:["codx-junior-max"]` merges the effort tier into the task, `clear:true` removes the schedule;
  - it **reads the task back** and reports the `wake_at` actually stored (no "I asked for it" answers).
- **Registered** in `api/codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` (import, `__all__`, `TOOLS` entry, tags `schedule/wake_at/after-hours`) — the `codx-junior` profile uses the `*` marker, so it gets it automatically.
- **Tests** in `api/tests/test_schedule_task_tool.py` (registration + time resolution incl. Madrid/CEST + garbage rejection).
- **Validation**: `python3 -m py_compile` on all three files → exit 0. `qa_run_tests` → **blocked, suite timeout** (900 s, then 240 s): `pytest:api` hangs even at collection and `pytest` is not installed in the `codx-junior-api` image. Recorded as next task, not hidden.

## Demo

Ask in a chat: *"schedule the chat-db task for tonight at 01:00 with max effort"* → the model calls `schedule_task(when="tonight 01:00", task="chat db…", profiles=["codx-junior-max"])` and you get back the stored `wake_at`. Static check of the tool itself:

```
docker exec codx-junior-api /usr/bin/python3 -m py_compile \
  /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/api/codx/junior/tools/schedule_task_tool.py
```

## Next tasks

1. `max` — **calendar projection M1**: tasks with `wake_at`/`due_date` rendered read-only in the `codx-junior` system calendar (`source='task'`, write attempts rejected) so a 01:00 run is *visible*.
2. `max` — **`wake_at` picker in the task editor/card** (presets Tonight 01:00 / Tomorrow 01:00 / +2 days / Custom + "scheduled" chip) so scheduling isn't agent-only.
3. `quick` — fix the QA gate (`pytest:api` hangs, no pytest in the api image, `max_test_seconds`) and delete my throw-away `tmp/_check_schedule_task.py`.

**Good enough?** ok / next / what is wrong

"""
Autonomous agents tools.

A profile becomes an **agent** when its ``autonomy`` block is enabled: it gets a
board of its own, a cadence and a mandate, and the autonomy worker wakes it on
schedule so it works without a human in the loop (see
:mod:`codx.junior.autonomy`).

This tool is the single entry point for that surface:

    - ``list`` / ``status`` : who the agents are, their board, cadence, cost and
                              next wake.
    - ``enable`` / ``disable`` : switch autonomy on/off for a profile.
    - ``configure``         : change the cadence, the mandate (standing orders),
                              the budget, the mode or the board.
    - ``wake``              : ask for a shift now (or at ``when``), e.g. after a
                              user leaves a note on the agent board.
    - ``schedule``          : set the next shift instant (``"+2d"``, ``"3 hours"``).
    - ``run``               : run a shift synchronously (blocking; for debugging).

Design notes:
    - **The profile is the agent.** There is no second catalogue: the
      configuration lives in ``.codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.profile`` under the
      ``autonomy`` key, so an agent inherits the whole profile machinery
      (linked profiles, tools, knowledge, model) instead of duplicating it. This
      is what lets an agent link the ``codx-junior`` profile and get the full
      workspace capabilities with initiative on top.
    - **Scheduling is a task field.** ``AutonomyService`` only wakes an agent for
      tasks whose ``Chat.wake_at`` is due, so an agent (or a human) schedules a
      follow-up by creating/updating a task with ``wake_at``.

def to_profile_names(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize a profile list: no duplicates, no leading ``@``.

    The chat engine re-emits profiles as ``@name`` mentions, so a stored
    ``@name`` (or ``@@name``) would never resolve to a profile. Only the values
    received are used — profiles are never inherited from the parent chat.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        De-duplicated profile names, order preserved.

    Example:
        >>> to_profile_names(["@backend", "backend", " ui "])
        ['backend', 'ui']
    """
    names: List[str] = []
    for name in to_list(value):
        clean = name.lstrip("@").strip()
        if clean and clean not in names:
            names.append(clean)
    return names


def to_wake_at(value: Any) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Normalize a scheduling expression into an ISO-8601 instant.

    Accepts the same vocabulary as the autonomy runtime (``"+2d"``, ``"3 hours"``,
    an ISO date or instant) so any task creation path can schedule a follow-up for
    an autonomous agent. An unparsable value schedules nothing instead of
    raising: a task must never be lost because of a bad date.

    Args:
        value: Scheduling expression.

    Returns:
        ISO instant, or None when there is nothing to schedule.

    Example:
        >>> to_wake_at("+2d")  # doctest: +SKIP
        '2026-04-03T00:00:00+00:00'
    """
    text = str(value if value is not None else "").strip()
    if not text:
        return None
    try:
        from codx.junior.autonomy.models import parse_when

        return parse_when(text) or None
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - scheduling is best effort
        logger.warning("TaskManager: cannot parse wake_at '%s': %s", text, ex)
        return None


def to_progress(value: Any, default: int = 0) -> int:
    """
    Clamp a completion percentage into the ``0-100`` range.

    Args:
        value: Raw progress value (may be None or a string).
        default: Value returned when ``value`` is not a number.

    Returns:
        Integer percentage.
    """
    try:
        return max(0, min(100, int(value)))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default

"""
Schedule task tool: put a task "for later" (after hours).

``wake_at`` already exists as a task field: it is the alarm clock the autonomy
worker reads, so a task carrying a due ``wake_at`` is picked up by the actor
owning its board without a human in the loop. Until now the field was reachable
from ``project_manager`` (create/update) and from the API, which means the model
had to know it existed to use it. This tool is the natural-language entry point
for the very same field:

    "schedule the chat-db task for tonight at 01:00, max effort"

Design notes:
    - **One field, one tool.** ``schedule_task`` never invents state: it writes
      ``Chat.wake_at`` (plus, optionally, ``profiles``) through
      ``ChatManager.update_chat_metadata``, exactly like ``project_manager``.
    - **Schedule an existing task or create one on the fly.** With ``task_id``
      (or ``task``, a name match) the task is rescheduled; with ``name`` +
      ``description`` a new task is created already scheduled.
    - **Off-hours vocabulary.** ``"01:00"``, ``"tonight 01:00"``,
      ``"tomorrow 1am"``, ``"after hours"`` (defaults to 01:00), ``"+2d"``,
      ``"3 hours"``, ``"2026-04-03"`` and ISO instants are accepted. Clock times
      are resolved in ``timezone`` (UTC by default) to the next occurrence, so
      "01:00" said at 15:00 means tonight, not thirteen hours ago.
    - **Read-back.** The tool returns the value stored in the task, so the model
      reports what happened instead of what it asked for.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
import re
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, List, Optional

from codx.junior.autonomy.models import timezone_for, utcnow
from codx.junior.task_manager import TaskManager, to_profile_names, to_wake_at
from .model import ToolResponse
from .project_manager_tools import _resolve_settings, validate_task_destination

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from codx.junior.settings import CODXJuniorSettings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Used when the caller only says "after hours"/"tonight" without a clock time.
DEFAULT_OFF_HOURS = "01:00"

_CLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"^(?:at\s+|@\s*)?(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm)?$", re.I)

_NIGHT_WORDS = ("tonight", "after hours", "after work", "overnight", "at night", "night")
_DAY_WORDS = ("tomorrow",)


def _strip_when_words(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove the natural-language prefix ("tonight", "tomorrow at", ...)."""
    cleaned = text
    for word in _NIGHT_WORDS + _DAY_WORDS:
        cleaned = re.sub(rf"^{word}\b[,\s]*", "", cleaned, flags=re.I)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"^(?:at|@)\s*", "", cleaned, flags=re.I)
    return cleaned.strip()


def _resolve_when(
    when: str,
    timezone_name: Optional[str] = None,
    now: Optional[Any] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Resolve a scheduling expression into an ISO-8601 UTC instant.

    Clock times (``"01:00"``, ``"tonight 01:00"``, ``"tomorrow 1am"``) are
    resolved to the *next* occurrence in ``timezone_name`` (UTC by default).
    Everything else is delegated to
    :func:`codx.junior.task_manager.to_wake_at`, which understands relative
    expressions (``"+2d"``, ``"3 hours"``), ISO dates and ISO instants.

    Args:
        when: The expression written by the user/model.
        timezone_name: IANA zone used to interpret clock times (``None`` = UTC).
        now: Reference instant, for tests.

    Returns:
        ISO-8601 UTC instant.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the expression cannot be understood.

    Example:
        >>> _resolve_when("12 hours")  # doctest: +SKIP
        '2026-04-01T22:00:00+00:00'
    """
    text = str(when or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise ValueError(
            "schedule_task requires 'when': '01:00', 'tonight 01:00', "
            "'tomorrow 1am', 'after hours', '+2d', '3 hours' or an ISO instant"
        )

    lowered = text.lower()
    tonight = any(word in lowered for word in _NIGHT_WORDS)
    tomorrow = any(word in lowered for word in _DAY_WORDS)
    cleaned = _strip_when_words(lowered)
    if not cleaned and tonight:
        cleaned = DEFAULT_OFF_HOURS

    clock = _CLOCK_RE.match(cleaned)
    if clock:
        hour = int(clock.group(1))
        minute = int(clock.group(2) or 0)
        meridiem = (clock.group(3) or "").lower()
        if meridiem == "pm" and hour < 12:
            hour += 12
        if meridiem == "am" and hour == 12:
            hour = 0
        if not (0 <= hour <= 23 and 0 <= minute <= 59):
            raise ValueError(f"schedule_task: '{when}' is not a valid clock time")
        zone = timezone_for(timezone_name)
        reference = (now or utcnow()).astimezone(zone)
        moment = reference.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0)
        # "01:00" at 15:00 means tonight (tomorrow 01:00), not 14 hours ago.
        if tomorrow or moment <= reference:
            moment = moment + timedelta(days=1)
        return moment.astimezone(reference.tzinfo).astimezone().isoformat()

    resolved = to_wake_at(text)
    if not resolved:
        raise ValueError(
            f"schedule_task: cannot understand when='{text}'. Use a clock time "
            "('01:00', 'tonight 01:00', 'tomorrow 1am'), a relative expression "
            "('+2d', '3 hours'), an ISO date ('2026-04-03') or an ISO instant."
        )
    return resolved


def _find_task(chat_manager: Any, task_id: Optional[str], task: Optional[str]) -> Any:
    """
    Load the task to reschedule by id, falling back to a name match.

    Args:
        chat_manager: The project chat manager.
        task_id: Task id (preferred).
        task: Task name (exact first, then substring, case insensitive).

    Returns:
        The :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat` task.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When no task matches or the name is ambiguous.
    """
    if task_id and str(task_id).strip():
        chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat_id=str(task_id).strip())
        if chat is None:
            raise ValueError(f"schedule_task: task '{task_id}' does not exist")
        return chat

    wanted = str(task or "").strip().lower()
    if not wanted:
        raise ValueError(
            "schedule_task requires 'task_id' (or 'task' name), or 'name' + "
            "'description' to create an already scheduled task"
        )

    chats = list(chat_manager.list_chats() or [])
    exact = [c for c in chats if (c.name or "").strip().lower() == wanted]
    matches = exact or [c for c in chats if wanted in (c.name or "").strip().lower()]
    if not matches:
        raise ValueError(f"schedule_task: no task matches '{task}'")
    if len(matches) > 1:
        listing = ", ".join(f"`{c.id}` ({c.name})" for c in matches[:10])
        raise ValueError(
            f"schedule_task: '{task}' is ambiguous, pass 'task_id': {listing}"
        )
    return matches[0]


def _merge_profiles(current: Any, extra: Optional[List[str]]) -> Optional[List[str]]:
    """Merge the requested profiles into the task list (order preserved)."""
    wanted = to_profile_names(extra)
    if not wanted:
        return None
    merged = to_profile_names(list(current or []) + wanted)
    return merged or None

            "Writes the task 'wake_at' field (the alarm clock the autonomy worker "
            "reads; it is NOT a deadline - use due_date for that). "
            "Either reschedule an existing task ('task_id' or 'task' name) or "
            "create one already scheduled ('name' + 'description'). "
            "'when' accepts '01:00', 'tonight 01:00', 'tomorrow 1am', "

``wake_at`` already exists as a task field: it is the alarm clock the autonomy

owning its board without a human in the loop. Until now the field was reachable
from ``project_manager`` (create/update) and from the API, which means the model
had to know it existed to use it. This tool is the natural-language entry point
for the very same field:

    "schedule the chat-db task for tonight at 01:00, max effort"

    - **One field, one tool.** ``schedule_task`` never invents state: it writes
      ``Chat.wake_at`` (plus, optionally, ``profiles``) through
      ``ChatManager.update_chat_metadata``, exactly like ``project_manager``.
    - **Schedule an existing task or create one on the fly.** With ``task_id``
      (or ``task``, a name match) the task is rescheduled; with ``name`` +
      ``description`` a new task is created already scheduled.
    - **Off-hours vocabulary.** ``"01:00"``, ``"tonight 01:00"``,
      ``"tomorrow 1am"``, ``"after hours"`` (defaults to 01:00), ``"+2d"``,
      ``"3 hours"``, ``"2026-04-03"`` and ISO instants are accepted. Clock times
      are resolved in ``timezone`` (UTC by default) to the next occurrence, so
      "01:00" said at 15:00 means tonight, not thirteen hours ago.

      reports what happened instead of what it asked for.

DEFAULT_OFF_HOURS = "01:00"

_CLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"^(?:at\s+|@\s*)?(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm)?$", re.I)

_NIGHT_WORDS = ("tonight", "after hours", "after work", "overnight", "at night", "night")
_DAY_WORDS = ("tomorrow",)


def _strip_when_words(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove the natural-language prefix ("tonight", "tomorrow at", ...)."""
    cleaned = text
    for word in _NIGHT_WORDS + _DAY_WORDS:
        cleaned = re.sub(rf"^{word}\b[,\s]*", "", cleaned, flags=re.I)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"^(?:at|@)\s*", "", cleaned, flags=re.I)
    return cleaned.strip()

    when: str,
    timezone_name: Optional[str] = None,
    now: Optional[Any] = None,

    """
    Resolve a scheduling expression into an ISO-8601 UTC instant.

    Clock times (``"01:00"``, ``"tonight 01:00"``, ``"tomorrow 1am"``) are
    resolved to the *next* occurrence in ``timezone_name`` (UTC by default).
    Everything else is delegated to
    :func:`codx.junior.task_manager.to_wake_at`, which understands relative
    expressions (``"+2d"``, ``"3 hours"``), ISO dates and ISO instants.

        when: The expression written by the user/model.
        timezone_name: IANA zone used to interpret clock times (``None`` = UTC).
        now: Reference instant, for tests.

    Returns:

        ValueError: When the expression cannot be understood.

    Example:

        '2026-04-01T22:00:00+00:00'
    """
    text = str(when or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise ValueError(
            "schedule_task requires 'when': '01:00', 'tonight 01:00', "
            "'tomorrow 1am', 'after hours', '+2d', '3 hours' or an ISO instant"
        )

    lowered = text.lower()
    tonight = any(word in lowered for word in _NIGHT_WORDS)
    tomorrow = any(word in lowered for word in _DAY_WORDS)
    cleaned = _strip_when_words(lowered)
    if not cleaned and tonight:
        cleaned = DEFAULT_OFF_HOURS

    clock = _CLOCK_RE.match(cleaned)
    if clock:

        minute = int(clock.group(2) or 0)

        moment = reference.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0)

        if tomorrow or moment <= reference:
            moment = moment + timedelta(days=1)

    resolved = to_wake_at(text)

            "('01:00', 'tonight 01:00', 'tomorrow 1am'), a relative expression "
            "('+2d', '3 hours'), an ISO date ('2026-04-03') or an ISO instant."

    Args:

            "'description' to create an already scheduled task"

    if not matches:

    if len(matches) > 1:

        raise ValueError(

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool allowlist sentinels
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A profile whose ``tools`` allowlist contains this marker is granted EVERY
# chat-scoped tool registered in the runtime (the "codx-junior" harness profile
# uses it). The marker is expanded where the request tools are decided
# (:class:`codx.junior.ai.smol.smol_agent.SmolAgent`), so it never reaches the
# provider. Validators accept it as a tool name so a profile saved with it
# keeps working.
ALL_TOOLS_MARKER = "*"

# Tools that are NEVER granted by an allowlist, even with the marker: they are
# injected per run by the agent, which is the only component that knows whether
# the user may teach a profile (write access) or must only read knowledge.
PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES = frozenset({
    "profile_learning",
    "profile_knowledge",
    "profile_knowledge_search",
})


def all_tool_names() -> frozenset:
    """Return the names of every tool registered in the runtime."""
    return frozenset(tool["tool_json"]["function"]["name"] for tool in TOOLS)


def expand_tool_allowlist(selected) -> frozenset:
    """
    Expand a tool-name allowlist (e.g. ``Profile.tools``) into a name set.

    * ``ALL_TOOLS_MARKER`` ("*") grants every registered tool.
    * ``PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES`` are never granted by an allowlist: they
      are injected per run by the agent, which is the only component that
      knows whether the user may teach a profile (write access) or must only
      read knowledge.

    Args:
        selected: Iterable of tool names (may contain the marker).

    Returns:
        Frozen set of concrete tool names.
    """
    names = {str(name) for name in (selected or []) if name}
    if ALL_TOOLS_MARKER in names:
        names.discard(ALL_TOOLS_MARKER)
        names.update(all_tool_names() - PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES)
    return frozenset(names)

"""
Tests for the ``schedule_task`` tool (after-hours task scheduling).

The tests cover the two things that can silently break: the natural-language
time resolution (which must never schedule something in the past) and the tool
registration (an unregistered tool is invisible to every profile).
"""

from datetime import datetime, timezone

import pytest

from codx.junior.tools import TOOLS, all_tool_names
from codx.junior.tools.schedule_task_tool import _resolve_when

NOW = datetime(2026, 4, 1, 15, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def _entry():
    for entry in TOOLS:
        if (entry.get("tool_json") or {}).get("function", {}).get("name") == "schedule_task":
            return entry
    return None


def test_schedule_task_is_registered():
    """The tool name and its callable are part of the runtime catalogue."""
    assert "schedule_task" in all_tool_names()
    entry = _entry()
    assert entry is not None
    assert entry["tool_call"].__name__ == "schedule_task"
    assert "wake_at" in (entry.get("tags") or [])


def test_schedule_task_tool_json_declares_when():
    """'when' is mandatory so the model cannot schedule without a moment."""
    parameters = _entry()["tool_json"]["function"]["parameters"]
    assert parameters["required"] == ["when"]
    for field in ("task_id", "task", "name", "profiles", "timezone", "clear"):
        assert field in parameters["properties"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "when,expected",
    [
        # A clock time already passed today means tonight, never the past.
        ("01:00", "2026-04-02T01:00:00+00:00"),
        ("tonight 01:00", "2026-04-02T01:00:00+00:00"),
        ("after hours", "2026-04-02T01:00:00+00:00"),
        ("tomorrow 1am", "2026-04-02T01:00:00+00:00"),
        ("at 23:30", "2026-04-01T23:30:00+00:00"),
    ],
)
def test_resolve_when_clock_times(when, expected):
    """Clock expressions resolve to the next occurrence in UTC by default."""
    assert _resolve_when(when, now=NOW) == expected


def test_resolve_when_uses_the_given_timezone():
    """'01:00' in Europe/Madrid is 23:00 UTC during CEST."""
    assert (
        _resolve_when("01:00", timezone_name="Europe/Madrid", now=NOW)
        == "2026-04-01T23:00:00+00:00"
    )


def test_resolve_when_delegates_relative_and_iso():
    """Relative expressions and ISO instants keep working."""
    assert _resolve_when("+2d", now=NOW) == "2026-04-03T15:00:00+00:00"
    assert _resolve_when("2026-05-01T09:30:00", now=NOW) == "2026-05-01T09:30:00+00:00"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("when", ["", "   ", "banana", "at 25:99"])
def test_resolve_when_rejects_garbage(when):
    """An unparsable schedule is an error, never a silent no-op."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _resolve_when(when, now=NOW)

"""Throw-away self-check for the schedule_task tool (no pytest needed)."""

import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/api")

from codx.junior.tools.schedule_task_tool import _resolve_when  # noqa: E402
from codx.junior.tools import TOOLS, all_tool_names  # noqa: E402

NOW = datetime(2026, 4, 1, 15, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

cases = [
    ("01:00", None, "2026-04-02T01:00:00+00:00"),
    ("tonight 01:00", None, "2026-04-02T01:00:00+00:00"),
    ("after hours", None, "2026-04-02T01:00:00+00:00"),
    ("tomorrow 1am", None, "2026-04-02T01:00:00+00:00"),
    ("at 23:30", None, "2026-04-01T23:30:00+00:00"),
    ("01:00", "Europe/Madrid", "2026-04-01T23:00:00+00:00"),
    ("+2d", None, "2026-04-03T15:00:00+00:00"),
    ("2026-05-01T09:30:00", None, "2026-05-01T09:30:00+00:00"),
]
failures = []
for when, tz, expected in cases:
    got = _resolve_when(when, timezone_name=tz, now=NOW)
    status = "ok" if got == expected else "FAIL"
    if got != expected:
        failures.append((when, tz, expected, got))
    print(f"{status}  when={when!r} tz={tz} -> {got}")

for bad in ["", "   ", "banana", "at 25:99"]:
    try:
        _resolve_when(bad, now=NOW)
        failures.append((bad, "should have raised", "", ""))
        print(f"FAIL  when={bad!r} did not raise")
    except ValueError:
        print(f"ok    when={bad!r} rejected")

assert "schedule_task" in all_tool_names(), "tool not registered"
entry = next(
    (
        item
        for item in TOOLS
        if (item.get("tool_json") or {}).get("function", {}).get("name") == "schedule_task"
    ),
    None,
)
assert entry is not None, "TOOLS entry missing"
assert entry["tool_call"].__name__ == "schedule_task"
assert entry["tool_json"]["function"]["parameters"]["required"] == ["when"]
print("ok    registered in TOOLS with required=['when']")

print("\nFAILURES:", failures or "none")
sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

            "can_write": self.can_write(calendar),
            "can_share": self.can_share(calendar),
            "read_only": calendar.is_read_only,
        }

    def _timezone(self) -> str:
        """
        Return the timezone used to describe the queried range.

        Resolution order: the viewer's preference, the project settings (when
        they ever carry one) and the first visible calendar's timezone.
        """
        preferred = self.get_prefs().get("timezone") or getattr(
            self.settings, "timezone", None
        )
        if preferred:
            return str(preferred)
        for calendar in self.visible_calendars():
            if calendar.timezone:
                return calendar.timezone
        return DEFAULT_TIMEZONE

    # -- calendars: read ---------------------------------------------------

    def get_calendar(self, calendar_id: str) -> Calendar:
        """
        Return one calendar the viewer may see.

        Args:
            calendar_id: Calendar id.

        Returns:
            The calendar.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 404 when the calendar does not exist **or** the
                viewer may not know it exists (§11.1: the two answers are
                deliberately identical).
        """
        calendar = self._calendars_by_id().get(str(calendar_id or "").strip())
        if calendar is None or not self.can_view(calendar):
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_NOT_FOUND, f"calendar '{calendar_id}' not found", 404
            )
        return calendar

    def orphan_events(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        List the events that point to a calendar which no longer exists.

        Invariant 1 of §3.2 says a dangling id is *reported for repair* by
        ``GET /calendars?orphans=1``, never silently dropped.

        Returns:
            ``[{event_id, title, calendar_ids}]`` for every event with at least
            one unknown membership.
        """
        known = set(self._calendars_by_id())
        orphans: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for event in self._iter_events():
            if not self.can_view_event(event):
                continue
            dangling = [cid for cid in event.calendar_ids if cid not in known]
            if dangling:
                orphans.append(
                    {
                        "event_id": event.id,
                        "title": event.title,
                        "calendar_ids": dangling,
                    }
                )
        return orphans

    # -- calendars: write --------------------------------------------------

    def _require_owner(self, calendar: Calendar) -> None:
        """Raise 403 unless the viewer may change the calendar itself."""
        if self.can_share(calendar):
            return
        raise CalendarError(
            ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
            f"only the owner of '{calendar.name}' or an administrator may change it",
            403,
        )

    def create_calendar(self, payload: CalendarCreate) -> Calendar:
        """
        Create a calendar owned by the viewer (§5.1).

        Args:
            payload: Calendar to create.

        Returns:
            The persisted calendar.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 403 for a ``workspace`` calendar requested by a
                non-admin, 409 for a ``system``/``external`` scope (they are
                materialised, never created by hand) or for an incomplete team
                audience.
        """
        if not self.username:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR, "authentication required", 403
            )
        if payload.scope in READ_ONLY_SCOPES:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
                f"'{payload.scope}' calendars are materialised, not created",
                409,
            )
        if payload.scope == "workspace" and not self.is_admin:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
                "only an installation administrator can create a workspace calendar",
                403,
            )

        audience = dict(payload.audience or {})
        if payload.scope == "workspace":
            audience["kind"] = "workspace"
        elif payload.scope == "team":
            audience["kind"] = "team"
            if not str(audience.get("name") or "").strip():
                raise CalendarError(
                    ERROR_INVALID_EVENT,
                    "a team calendar needs audience.name (the team name)",
                    400,
                )
            audience["members"] = _dedupe(
                audience.get("members") or [self.username]
            )
        else:
            audience = None

        calendar = Calendar(
            name=payload.name,
            color=payload.color,
            description=payload.description,
            scope=payload.scope,
            owner=self.username,
            audience=audience,
            timezone=payload.timezone or DEFAULT_TIMEZONE,
            default_reminders=payload.default_reminders or [],
            members=[CalendarMember(user=self.username, role="owner")],
            visible=payload.visible,
            order=payload.order,
        )
        saved = self.store.save_calendar(calendar)
        self._invalidate()
        return saved

    def update_calendar(self, calendar_id: str, payload: CalendarUpdate) -> Calendar:
        """
        Partially update a calendar the viewer owns (or administers).

        Args:
            calendar_id: Calendar id.
            payload: Only the fields that were sent are applied.

        Returns:
            The persisted calendar.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 404 unknown/invisible calendar, 403 not the owner,
                409 on a read-only calendar or when escalating the scope to
                ``workspace`` without being an admin.
        """
        calendar = self.get_calendar(calendar_id)
        self._require_owner(calendar)
        if calendar.is_read_only:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
                f"'{calendar.name}' is read-only",
                409,
            )

        changes = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
        new_scope = changes.get("scope")
        if new_scope and new_scope != calendar.scope:
            if new_scope in READ_ONLY_SCOPES:
                raise CalendarError(
                    ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
                    f"'{new_scope}' calendars are materialised, not created",
                    409,
                )
            if new_scope == "workspace" and not self.is_admin:
                raise CalendarError(
                    ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
                    "only an installation administrator can create a workspace calendar",
                    403,
                )

        try:
            updated = Calendar(**{**calendar.model_dump(), **changes})
        except ValidationError as ex:
            raise CalendarError(ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, str(ex), 400) from ex
        saved = self.store.save_calendar(updated)
        self._invalidate()
        return saved

    def delete_calendar(
        self, calendar_id: str, move_to: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> Calendar:
        """
        Delete a calendar, refusing to orphan its events (§5.1).

        Args:
            calendar_id: Calendar id.
            move_to: Calendar that inherits the events of the deleted one.

        Returns:
            The deleted calendar document.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 404 unknown/invisible calendar, 403 not the owner,
                409 when it is read-only or still holds events and ``move_to``
                was not given, 404 when ``move_to`` does not resolve.
        """
        calendar = self.get_calendar(calendar_id)
        self._require_owner(calendar)
        if calendar.is_read_only:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR, f"'{calendar.name}' is read-only", 409
            )

        references = [
            event for event in self._iter_events() if calendar.id in event.calendar_ids
        ]
        target: Optional[Calendar] = None
        if references and not move_to:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_CALENDAR_IN_USE,
                f"'{calendar.name}' still holds {len(references)} event(s); "
                "pass move_to to move them",
                409,
            )
        if move_to:
            target = self.get_calendar(move_to)
            if target.id == calendar.id:
                raise CalendarError(
                    ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, "move_to must be a different calendar", 400
                )
            if not self.can_write(target):
                raise CalendarError(
                    ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
                    f"'{target.name}' is not writable for '{self.username}'",
                    403,
                )
            for event in references:
                event.calendar_ids = _dedupe(
                    target.id if cid == calendar.id else cid
                    for cid in event.calendar_ids
                )
                event.revision += 1
                self.store.save_event(event)

        self.store.delete_calendar(calendar.id)
        self._invalidate()
        return calendar

    # -- projects (the filter bar) ----------------------------------------

    def projects(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return the projects the viewer may put events in (§5.1).

        Reuses the existing project discovery (``find_all_user_projects`` for
        everybody else, ``find_all_projects`` for an administrator), so the
        filter never offers a project the caller cannot open.

        Returns:
            ``[{project_id, name, role}]`` sorted by name.
        """
        entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        try:
            from codx.junior.project.project_discover import (
                find_all_projects,
                find_all_user_projects,
            )
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - discovery must never break
            logger.warning("calendar: project discovery unavailable: %s", ex)
            return entries

        try:
            if self.is_admin:
                settings_list = list((find_all_projects() or {}).values())
                role_for = lambda _settings: USER_ROLE_ADMIN  # noqa: E731
            elif self.user is not None:
                settings_list = list(find_all_user_projects(self.user))
                role_for = lambda settings: (  # noqa: E731
                    getattr(settings, "permissions", "") or USER_ROLE_USER
                )
            else:
                settings_list = []
                role_for = lambda _settings: USER_ROLE_USER  # noqa: E731
        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - never break the filter bar
            logger.error("calendar: project discovery failed: %s", ex)
            return entries

        seen: List[str] = []
        for settings in settings_list:
            project_id = getattr(settings, "project_id", None)
            if not project_id or project_id in seen:
                continue
            seen.append(project_id)
            entries.append(
                {
                    "project_id": project_id,
                    "name": getattr(settings, "project_name", None) or project_id,
                    "role": role_for(settings),
                }
            )
        entries.sort(key=lambda entry: str(entry["name"]).lower())
        return entries

    # -- preferences -------------------------------------------------------

    def get_prefs(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Return the caller's preferences (hidden calendars, order, week start).

        A missing or unreadable document degrades to the defaults instead of
        failing the request: preferences are a convenience, not data.

        Returns:
            The preferences document, completed with the defaults.
        """
        prefs: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "hidden_calendars": [],
            "order": {},
            "week_start": DEFAULT_WEEK_START,
        }
        if not self.username:
            return prefs
        try:
            stored = self.store.get_prefs(self.username)
        except (ValueError, OSError) as ex:
            logger.warning("calendar: cannot read prefs of '%s': %s", self.username, ex)
            return prefs
        if isinstance(stored, dict):
            prefs.update(stored)
        return prefs

    def save_prefs(self, payload: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Persist the caller's preferences.

        Args:
            payload: The (partial) preferences document; unknown keys are kept
                as they are so a later milestone can extend the file.

        Returns:
            The stored document.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 400 when a known key has an invalid value.
        """
        if not self.username:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR, "authentication required", 403
            )
        prefs = {**self.get_prefs(), **dict(payload or {})}
        if not isinstance(prefs.get("hidden_calendars"), (list, tuple)):
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, "hidden_calendars must be a list", 400
            )
        prefs["hidden_calendars"] = _dedupe(prefs.get("hidden_calendars"))
        if not isinstance(prefs.get("order"), dict):
            raise CalendarError(ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, "order must be an object", 400)
        try:
            prefs["order"] = {
                str(key): int(value) for key, value in prefs["order"].items()
            }
        except (TypeError, ValueError) as ex:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, "order values must be integers", 400
            ) from ex
        week_start = str(prefs.get("week_start") or DEFAULT_WEEK_START).lower()
        if week_start not in WEEK_STARTS:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_EVENT,
                f"week_start must be one of {', '.join(WEEK_STARTS)}",
                400,
            )
        prefs["week_start"] = week_start
        return self.store.save_prefs(self.username, prefs)

    # -- events: helpers ---------------------------------------------------

    def _iter_events(self) -> Iterator[CalendarEvent]:
        """Yield every stored event (all shards)."""
        for month in self.store.list_event_months():
            for event in self.store.list_events_month(month):
                yield event

    def _visible_memberships(self, event: CalendarEvent) -> List[str]:
        """Return the calendar ids of *event* the viewer may see."""
        by_id = self._calendars_by_id()
        return [
            calendar_id
            for calendar_id in event.calendar_ids
            if calendar_id in by_id and self.can_view(by_id[calendar_id])
        ]

    def can_view_event(self, event: Optional[CalendarEvent]) -> bool:
        """Tell whether the viewer sees at least one membership of *event*."""
        if event is None:
            return False
        return bool(self._visible_memberships(event))

    def _writable_memberships(self, calendar_ids: Iterable[str]) -> List[str]:
        """Return the calendar ids of *calendar_ids* the viewer may write."""
        by_id = self._calendars_by_id()
        return [
            calendar_id
            for calendar_id in _dedupe(calendar_ids)
            if calendar_id in by_id and self.can_write(by_id[calendar_id])
        ]

    @staticmethod
    def matches_projects(
        project_id: Optional[str], projects: Optional[Iterable[str]]
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Apply the ``projects[]`` filter to one item (§5.2).

        ``absent`` or ``[]`` → no filtering; ``"personal"`` matches a ``None``
        project; several tokens are **OR**-ed. Never AND.

        Args:
            project_id: Project of the item (``None`` = personal).
            projects: The filter tokens.

        Returns:
            ``True`` when the item belongs to the selection.

        Example:
            >>> CalendarService.matches_projects(None, ["personal"])
            True
            >>> CalendarService.matches_projects("acme-web", ["personal"])
            False
        """
        tokens = _dedupe(projects)
        if not tokens:
            return True
        for token in tokens:
            if token == PERSONAL_TOKEN:
                if not project_id:
                    return True
            elif project_id and project_id == token:
                return True
        return False

    def _is_masked(self, event: CalendarEvent, calendar_ids: List[str]) -> bool:
        """
        Tell whether the details of *event* must be hidden from the viewer.

        An event with ``visibility: private`` keeps its slot but masks its
        title, description, location and guests for anybody who is neither its
        creator nor a writer of one of its calendars (§11.1).
        """
        if event.visibility != "private":
            return False
        if event.created_by and event.created_by == self.username:
            return False
        by_id = self._calendars_by_id()
        return not any(
            by_id[calendar_id].member_role(self.username) in WRITE_ROLES
            for calendar_id in calendar_ids
            if calendar_id in by_id
        )

    def _occurrence(
        self, event: CalendarEvent, calendar_ids: List[str]
    ) -> Occurrence:
        """
        Build the single occurrence of *event* inside the visible memberships.

        M0 does not expand recurrences: a recurring event yields exactly one
        occurrence at its stored start (M3 expands the rule).
        """
        hidden = set(self.hidden_calendar_ids())
        primary = next(
            (cid for cid in calendar_ids if cid not in hidden), calendar_ids[0]
        )
        masked = self._is_masked(event, calendar_ids)
        return Occurrence(
            event_id=event.id,
            calendar_ids=calendar_ids,
            project_id=event.project_id,
            title="Private" if masked else event.title,
            start=event.start,
            end=event.end or event.start,
            all_day=event.all_day,
            source=event.source,
            refs={} if masked else dict(event.refs or {}),
            calendar_id=primary,
            is_recurring_instance=False,
            original_start=None,
            overdue=False,
            read_only=not self._writable_memberships(calendar_ids),
        )

    # -- events: query -----------------------------------------------------

    def query(self, query: EventQuery) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Answer the main read of the agenda (§5.2).

        The pipeline is fixed: **visibility** (ACL) → **calendars[]** →
        **hidden** calendars → **projects[]** → **sources[]** → **q** →
        occurrences. The project filter is applied after visibility so a token
        can never widen what the viewer sees.

        Args:
            query: The validated request payload.

        Returns:
            ``{range, calendars, projects, occurrences, counts, warnings,
            truncated_projects}``.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 400 ``invalid_range`` when the window is reversed or
                wider than :data:`MAX_QUERY_DAYS` (§12 guard rail).
        """
        start_dt = parse_iso(query.from_)
        end_dt = parse_iso(query.to)
        if start_dt is None or end_dt is None:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_RANGE,
                f"invalid range: from={query.from_!r} to={query.to!r}",
                400,
            )
        if end_dt <= start_dt:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_RANGE, "the range end must be after its start", 400
            )
        if end_dt - start_dt > timedelta(days=MAX_QUERY_DAYS):
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_RANGE,
                f"the range is {(end_dt - start_dt).days} days wide, "
                f"the maximum is {MAX_QUERY_DAYS}",
                400,
            )

        warnings: List[str] = []
        calendars = self.visible_calendars()
        by_id = {calendar.id: calendar for calendar in calendars}
        hidden = set(self.hidden_calendar_ids())

        requested = _dedupe(query.calendar_ids)
        for calendar_id in requested:
            if calendar_id not in by_id:
                warnings.append(
                    f"{ERROR_UNKNOWN_CALENDAR}: '{calendar_id}' is not a visible calendar"
                )
        selected = [calendar_id for calendar_id in requested if calendar_id in by_id]
        if requested and not selected:
            calendars_in_response = calendars
        else:
            calendars_in_response = [
                calendar
                for calendar in calendars
                if not selected or calendar.id in selected
            ]

        sources = set(_dedupe(query.sources))
        needle = (query.q or "").strip().lower()

        occurrences: List[Occurrence] = []
        for event in self.store.list_events_range(query.from_, query.to):
            memberships = self._visible_memberships(event)
            if selected:
                memberships = [cid for cid in memberships if cid in selected]
            if not memberships:
                continue
            if not query.include_hidden and all(cid in hidden for cid in memberships):
                continue
            if sources and event.source not in sources:
                continue
            if not self.matches_projects(event.project_id, query.projects):
                continue
            if needle:
                haystack = " ".join(
                    [event.title or "", event.description or "", event.location or ""]
                ).lower()
                if needle not in haystack:
                    continue
            occurrences.append(self._occurrence(event, memberships))

        # M1 projection: the scheduled tasks of the project join the agenda as
        # read-only items of the system calendar, never as stored copies.
        occurrences.extend(
            self._task_occurrences(
                start_dt=start_dt,
                end_dt=end_dt,
                sources=sources,
                needle=needle,
                projects=query.projects,
                selected=selected,
                hidden=hidden,
                include_hidden=query.include_hidden,
            )
        )

        occurrences.sort(key=lambda item: (item.start or "", item.title or ""))

        by_calendar: Counter = Counter(item.calendar_id for item in occurrences)
        by_source: Counter = Counter(item.source for item in occurrences)
        by_project: Counter = Counter(
            item.project_id or PERSONAL_TOKEN for item in occurrences
        )

        return {
            "range": {
                "from": to_utc_iso(start_dt),
                "to": to_utc_iso(end_dt),
                "timezone": self._timezone(),
            },
            "calendars": [
                self.calendar_payload(calendar) for calendar in calendars_in_response
            ],
            "projects": sorted(by_project.keys()),
            "occurrences": [occurrence.model_dump() for occurrence in occurrences],
            "counts": {
                "by_calendar": dict(by_calendar),
                "by_source": dict(by_source),
                "by_project": dict(by_project),
            },
            "warnings": warnings,
            # The projection of the 'codx-junior' calendar is M1: no project is
            # read outside the global store yet, so nothing is ever truncated.
            "truncated_projects": [],
        }

    # -- events: read ------------------------------------------------------

    def event_payload(self, event: CalendarEvent) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Serialise an event for the API, masking what the viewer may not read.

        The memberships are reduced to the calendars the viewer may see, the
        details of a ``visibility: private`` event of somebody else are masked
        (the slot stays visible so overlapping meetings keep their place, §11.1)
        and ``can_write`` is resolved here instead of in the client.

        Args:
            event: Event to serialise.

        Returns:
            The event document plus ``can_write``.
        """
        memberships = self._visible_memberships(event) or list(event.calendar_ids)
        payload = event.model_dump()
        payload["calendar_ids"] = memberships
        if self._is_masked(event, memberships):
            payload.update(
                {"title": "Private", "description": "", "location": "", "guests": []}
            )
        payload["can_write"] = bool(self._writable_memberships(memberships))
        return payload

    def get_event(self, event_id: str) -> CalendarEvent:
        """
        Return the raw event document (the editor needs the rule, not the
        instances).

        Args:
            event_id: Event id.

        Returns:
            The stored event.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 404 when the event does not exist or none of its
                calendars is visible to the viewer.
        """
        event = self.store.get_event(str(event_id or "").strip())
        if not self.can_view_event(event):
            raise CalendarError(ERROR_NOT_FOUND, f"event '{event_id}' not found", 404)
        return event

    # -- events: validation ------------------------------------------------

    def _resolve_calendars(self, calendar_ids: Iterable[str]) -> List[Calendar]:
        """
        Resolve every calendar id of a write, rejecting unknown ones.

        Args:
            calendar_ids: Calendar ids the event must belong to.

        Returns:
            The resolved calendars.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 404 ``unknown_calendar`` for the first unresolvable
                id (an id the viewer cannot see is unresolvable, §11.1).
        """
        by_id = self._calendars_by_id()
        resolved: List[Calendar] = []
        for calendar_id in _dedupe(calendar_ids):
            calendar = by_id.get(calendar_id)
            if calendar is None or not self.can_view(calendar):
                raise CalendarError(
                    ERROR_UNKNOWN_CALENDAR,
                    f"'{calendar_id}' does not resolve to a calendar",
                    404,
                )
            resolved.append(calendar)
        return resolved

    def _require_writable(self, calendars: List[Calendar]) -> None:
        """
        Raise unless the viewer may write the event in at least one calendar.

        A write whose only calendars are ``system``/``external`` is refused with
        409 ``read_only_calendar`` (§3.2 invariant 2: projected content cannot be
        edited); a missing role is refused with 403 ``read_only_calendar``
        (§11.1: a ``reader`` cannot write).
        """
        if any(self.can_write(calendar) for calendar in calendars):
            return
        names = ", ".join(calendar.name for calendar in calendars) or "-"
        if all(calendar.is_read_only for calendar in calendars):
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
                f"'{names}' is read-only; projected items are moved in their source",
                409,
            )
        raise CalendarError(
            ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR,
            f"'{self.username}' cannot write '{names}'",
            403,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _normalize_times(start: str, end: Optional[str], all_day: bool) -> tuple:
        """
        Validate the time slot of an event and return it as a UTC pair.

        Enforces invariant 3 of §3.2 (``end > start``, all-day events default to
        one day) and the ``MAX_EVENT_DURATION_DAYS`` limit of §4.4.

        Args:
            start: Start, ISO-8601.
            end: End, ISO-8601 (``None`` for an all-day event).
            all_day: Whether the event is all-day.

        Returns:
            ``(start_iso, end_iso)`` normalised to UTC.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 400 ``invalid_event`` for a reversed slot or an
                unparsable date, 400 ``event_too_long`` beyond the limit.
        """
        start_dt = parse_iso(start)
        if start_dt is None:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, f"invalid start: {start!r}", 400
            )
        end_dt = parse_iso(end)
        if end_dt is None or end_dt <= start_dt:
            if not all_day:
                raise CalendarError(
                    ERROR_INVALID_EVENT,
                    f"end ({end!r}) must be after start ({start!r})",
                    400,
                )
            end_dt = start_dt + timedelta(days=1)
        if end_dt - start_dt > timedelta(days=MAX_EVENT_DURATION_DAYS):
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_EVENT_TOO_LONG,
                f"an event may last at most {MAX_EVENT_DURATION_DAYS} days; "
                "model a longer period as a recurring event",
                400,
            )
        return to_utc_iso(start_dt), to_utc_iso(end_dt)

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_recurrence(recurrence: Any) -> None:
        """
        Reject a recurrence rule that is not an RFC 5545 ``RRULE``.

        M0 stores the rule verbatim (expansion is M3), so the only check is the
        structural one: a rule must declare ``FREQ`` — anything else would be
        silently unexpandable later.
        """
        if recurrence is None:
            return
        if isinstance(recurrence, dict):
            rule = str(recurrence.get("rrule") or "").strip()
        else:
            rule = str(getattr(recurrence, "rrule", "") or "").strip()
        if rule and "FREQ=" not in rule.upper():
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_RECURRENCE,
                f"'{rule}' is not an RFC 5545 RRULE (missing FREQ)",
                400,
            )

    # -- events: write -----------------------------------------------------

    def create_event(self, payload: EventCreate) -> CalendarEvent:
        """
        Create an event (``calendar_ids[]`` required, §5.2).

        Args:
            payload: Event to create.

        Returns:
            The persisted event, ``revision`` 1.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: ``unknown_calendar`` (404), ``read_only_calendar``
                (403/409), ``invalid_event``, ``event_too_long`` or
                ``invalid_recurrence`` (400).
        """
        calendars = self._resolve_calendars(payload.calendar_ids)
        self._require_writable(calendars)
        start, end = self._normalize_times(payload.start, payload.end, payload.all_day)
        self._validate_recurrence(payload.recurrence)

        reminders = payload.reminders or []
        if not reminders:
            primary = next(
                (calendar for calendar in calendars if self.can_write(calendar)),
                calendars[0],
            )
            reminders = list(primary.default_reminders)

        event = CalendarEvent(
            calendar_ids=[calendar.id for calendar in calendars],
            project_id=payload.project_id,
            title=payload.title,
            description=payload.description,
            location=payload.location,
            start=start,
            end=end,
            all_day=payload.all_day,
            timezone=payload.timezone or DEFAULT_TIMEZONE,
            recurrence=payload.recurrence,
            reminders=reminders,
            status=payload.status,
            visibility=payload.visibility,
            source="native",
            refs=payload.refs or {},
            guests=payload.guests or [],
            created_by=self.username or None,
            revision=1,
        )
        try:
            saved = self.store.save_event(event)
        except ValidationError as ex:
            raise CalendarError(ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, str(ex), 400) from ex
        return saved

    def update_event(
        self,
        event_id: str,
        payload: EventUpdate,
        expected_revision: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> CalendarEvent:
        """
        Apply a partial update, guarded by the optimistic lock (§5.3).

        Args:
            event_id: Event id.
            payload: The fields to change.
            expected_revision: The ``If-Match`` revision; falls back to
                ``payload.revision`` when the header is absent.

        Returns:
            The persisted event with its incremented ``revision``.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 404 not found/invisible, 409 ``revision_mismatch``,
                ``unknown_calendar``, ``read_only_calendar``, ``invalid_event``,
                ``event_too_long`` or ``invalid_recurrence``.
        """
        current = self.get_event(event_id)
        changes = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
        expected = (
            expected_revision
            if expected_revision is not None
            else changes.pop("revision", None)
        )
        changes.pop("revision", None)
        if expected is not None and int(expected) != current.revision:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_REVISION_MISMATCH,
                f"the event is at revision {current.revision}, "
                f"your copy is {expected}",
                409,
            )

        merged = {**current.model_dump(), **changes}

        calendars = self._resolve_calendars(merged.get("calendar_ids") or [])
        # The viewer must be able to write both the old and the new memberships:
        # an event can never be moved *out* of a calendar it cannot write.
        self._require_writable(calendars)
        self._require_writable(
            self._resolve_calendars(self._visible_memberships(current))
        )

        start, end = self._normalize_times(
            merged.get("start"), merged.get("end"), bool(merged.get("all_day"))
        )
        merged["start"], merged["end"] = start, end
        self._validate_recurrence(merged.get("recurrence"))

        merged["revision"] = current.revision + 1
        try:
            event = CalendarEvent(**merged)
        except ValidationError as ex:
            raise CalendarError(ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, str(ex), 400) from ex
        return self.store.save_event(event)

    def delete_event(self, event_id: str, scope: str = "all") -> CalendarEvent:
        """
        Delete an event.

        ``scope`` keeps the Google semantics of §5.2 (``single`` | ``following``
        | ``all``). M0 does not expand recurrences, so only ``all`` is
        meaningful: deleting one instance or a suffix of a series needs the
        recurrence engine (M3) and is refused instead of silently deleting the
        whole series.

        Args:
            event_id: Event id.
            scope: ``single`` | ``following`` | ``all``.

        Returns:
            The deleted event document.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 404 not found/invisible, 403 not writable, 400 when a
                per-instance delete is requested on a recurring event.
        """
        event = self.get_event(event_id)
        scope = str(scope or "all").strip().lower()
        if scope not in ("single", "following", "all"):
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_EVENT,
                f"scope must be single, following or all (got '{scope}')",
                400,
            )
        if scope != "all" and event.is_recurring:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_RECURRENCE,
                "deleting a single instance of a recurring event arrives with "
                "the recurrence engine (M3); use scope=all",
                400,
            )
        self._require_writable(
            self._resolve_calendars(self._visible_memberships(event))
        )
        self.store.delete_event(event.id)
        return event

    # -- reminders (M2 owns the delivery) ---------------------------------

    def snooze(
        self,
        event_id: str,
        minutes: int,
        occurrence_start: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Validate a snooze request and answer the new trigger times.

        Reminder *delivery* is milestone M2: the background ticker and the
        durable ``delivered.json`` key do not exist yet, so this method
        deliberately persists nothing and says so (``persisted: false``). It
        still enforces the contract of §5.2 — the event must exist, be visible
        and be writable, and ``minutes`` must be sane — so the client can be
        built (and tested) against the final shape.

        Args:
            event_id: Event id.
            minutes: Minutes to postpone the reminder.
            occurrence_start: Occurrence whose reminder is snoozed; defaults to
                the stored ``start``.

        Returns:
            ``{event_id, occurrence_start, snooze_until, reminders, persisted}``.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 404 not found/invisible, 403 not writable, 400 for a
                non-positive or excessive delay.
        """
        event = self.get_event(event_id)
        try:
            delay = int(minutes)
        except (TypeError, ValueError) as ex:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, "minutes must be an integer", 400
            ) from ex
        if delay <= 0 or delay > MAX_SNOOZE_MINUTES:
            raise CalendarError(
                ERROR_INVALID_EVENT,
                f"minutes must be between 1 and {MAX_SNOOZE_MINUTES}",
                400,
            )
        self._require_writable(
            self._resolve_calendars(self._visible_memberships(event))
        )

        base = parse_iso(occurrence_start) or event.start_datetime() or datetime.now(
            timezone.utc
        )
        until = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(minutes=delay)
        return {
            "event_id": event.id,
            "occurrence_start": to_utc_iso(base),
            "snooze_until": to_utc_iso(until),
            "reminders": [
                {
                    "channel": reminder.channel,
                    "minutes_before": reminder.minutes_before,
                    "trigger_at": to_utc_iso(until),
                }
                for reminder in event.reminders
            ],
            "persisted": False,
        }

    # -- quick add ---------------------------------------------------------

    def quick_add(self, text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Parse ``"Lunch Ana tom 13:00 1h @Café"`` into a draft (§5.2).

        The draft is **never persisted**: it is a proposal the editor confirms.
        Recognised tokens: ``HH:MM`` or ``9am`` (time), ``1h`` / ``30m``
        (duration), ``@place`` (location), ``YYYY-MM-DD`` / ``today`` /
        ``tomorrow`` (day) and ``all day``. Everything else is the title.

        Args:
            text: The raw sentence typed by the user.

        Returns:
            ``{text, draft, persisted, warnings}`` where ``draft`` is a ready
            ``POST /api/calendar/events`` payload.

        Raises:
            CalendarError: 400 when the text is empty.
        """
        raw = str(text or "").strip()
        if not raw:
            raise CalendarError(ERROR_INVALID_EVENT, "text is required", 400)
        remaining = raw
        warnings: List[str] = []

        location = ""
        match = _QUICK_LOCATION.search(remaining)
        if match:
            location = match.group(1)
            remaining = _QUICK_LOCATION.sub(" ", remaining)

        day: Optional[date] = None
        match = _QUICK_DATE.search(remaining)
        if match:
            try:
                day = datetime.strptime(match.group(1), "%Y-%m-%d").date()
                remaining = _QUICK_DATE.sub(" ", remaining)
            except ValueError:
                warnings.append(f"ignored the date '{match.group(1)}'")

        lowered = remaining.lower()
        today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()
        for token in _DAY_TOKENS:
            if token in lowered:
                day = today + timedelta(days=1 if token == "tomorrow" else 0)
                remaining = re.sub(
                    rf"\b{token}\b", " ", remaining, flags=re.IGNORECASE
                )
                lowered = remaining.lower()
                break

        all_day = "all day" in lowered or "allday" in lowered
        if all_day:
            remaining = re.sub(r"\ball\s*day\b", " ", remaining, flags=re.IGNORECASE)

        duration = DEFAULT_EVENT_MINUTES
        match = _QUICK_DURATION.search(remaining)
        if match:
            amount = int(match.group(1))
            unit = match.group(2).lower()
            duration = amount * 60 if unit.startswith("h") else amount
            remaining = _QUICK_DURATION.sub(" ", remaining)

        hour: Optional[int] = None
        minute = 0
        match = _QUICK_TIME.search(remaining)
        if match and int(match.group(1)) < 24 and int(match.group(2)) < 60:
            hour, minute = int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2))
            remaining = _QUICK_TIME.sub(" ", remaining)
        else:
            match = _QUICK_MERIDIEM.search(remaining)
            if match:
                hour = int(match.group(1)) % 12
                if match.group(2).lower() == "pm":
                    hour += 12
                remaining = _QUICK_MERIDIEM.sub(" ", remaining)

        if hour is None:
            next_hour = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(hours=1)
            hour, minute = next_hour.hour, 0

        title = " ".join(remaining.split()) or "Untitled event"
        target_day = day or today
        start_dt = datetime(
            target_day.year,
            target_day.month,
            target_day.day,
            hour,
            minute,
            tzinfo=timezone.utc,
        )
        if all_day:
            start_dt = datetime(
                target_day.year, target_day.month, target_day.day, tzinfo=timezone.utc
            )
            end_dt = start_dt + timedelta(days=1)
        else:
            end_dt = start_dt + timedelta(minutes=duration)

        calendars = [
            calendar
            for calendar in self.visible_calendars()
            if self.can_write(calendar)
        ]
        calendar_ids = [calendars[0].id] if calendars else []
        if not calendar_ids:
            warnings.append(
                f"{ERROR_READ_ONLY_CALENDAR}: the viewer cannot write any calendar"
            )

        return {
            "text": raw,
            "persisted": False,
            "warnings": warnings,
            "draft": {
                "calendar_ids": calendar_ids,
                "title": title,
                "description": "",
                "location": location,
                "start": to_utc_iso(start_dt),
                "end": to_utc_iso(end_dt),
                "all_day": all_day,
                "timezone": self._timezone(),
                "project_id": None,
                "reminders": list(calendars[0].default_reminders) if calendars else [],
                "guests": [],
            },
        }
